key_insight: Thresholding extreme vorticity and reconstructing the flow via the Biot-Savart law lets the authors separate intermittency-driven effects from the underlying turbulent scaling laws.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to identify which turbulent statistics are robust to intermittency and which are dominated by intense coherent structures, useful for modeling and subgrid-scale analysis.
method: Threshold vorticity to remove extreme intermittent regions
Invert the Biot-Savart law to reconstruct filtered velocity fields
Compare spectra, structure functions, multifractality, and vortex-stretching metrics before and after filtering
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that as extreme vorticity is filtered out, the energy spectrum scaling persists while the bottleneck flattens, structure-function exponents move toward Kolmogorov values, and multifractality shrinks.
watch_item: Because the filtered fields become increasingly detached from the original turbulence skeleton, the method may alter physically important coherent-structure dynamics if the threshold is too aggressive.
paper_title: Disentangling intermittent flow structure contributions to anomalous scaling and multifractality in turbulence
